name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
use_case: A financial appraisal that expresses every expected cost and every expected benefit of an option in monetary terms over a defined horizon, discounts them to present value, and compares the resulting net figures across alternatives. Best used for capital expenditure, procurement and infrastructure choices that must be justified to a budget holder or an auditor, where an explicit money figure and a stated discount rate are required rather than a qualitative preference.
strengths: produces a defensible number for budget holders and auditors
the discount rate makes the time value of long payback periods explicit
forces hidden operating and decommissioning costs into the open
sensitivity analysis shows which single assumption drives the answer
weaknesses: systematically undervalues benefits that resist being priced
the result is only as good as the forecasts feeding it
small changes to the discount rate can flip the recommendation
invites motivated reasoning when the preferred answer is known in advance
use_cases: A town council has to choose between refurbishing its ageing swimming pool, building a new one or closing it, and the finance committee wants each option's lifetime costs and gains set against carrying on as now.
A regulator drafting a new rule has to show whether the gains to the public outweigh the compliance burden it puts on businesses and households.
A school board choosing between hiring reading tutors and cutting class sizes wants to compare what each costs per pupil with the long-run gains in attainment and later earnings.
A manufacturer considering automating a production line wants to know whether savings over the equipment's life justify the purchase once maintenance, retraining and downtime are counted.
